# Harrison

## Overview

- **Age:** Middle-aged, around 55  <sub>[v2 c1 P1](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0001), [v2 c1 P28](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0028), [v2 c23 P9](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0009)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive
- **Origin:** New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P43](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0043)</sub>
- **Role:** Farmer  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P12](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0012)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** J. A. Harrison  <sub>[v2 c1 P1](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0001), [v2 c1 P13](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0013)</sub>; James A.  <sub>[v2 c25 P11](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0011), [v2 c25 P12](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0012)</sub>

## Appearance

He is a short, fat, and bald man with prominent blue eyes and an ungainly, heavy-set frame. He is typically seen wearing working clothes, which are sometimes ragged or patched, and he often chews on a straw while relaxing. When shaved and trimmed, he presents a much sprucer appearance.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c3 P0](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0000), [v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000), [v2 c25 P46](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0046)_

## Personality

He is known throughout Avonlea as a blunt, outspoken, and irritable crank who prides himself on telling the disagreeable truth. Beneath his crusty, crabbed, and quick-tempered exterior, he possesses a kind, honest, and jovial nature that appreciates youth and neighborliness. Though he often grumbles about town affairs and dislikes meddlesome gossips, he is capable of great tolerance, humor, and generosity once his goodwill is earned.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P22](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0022), [v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025), [v2 c3 P40](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0040), [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049), [v2 c7 P10](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0010), [v2 c9 P5](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0005), [v2 c9 P9](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0009)_

## History

After the death of his sister in Scottsford, New Brunswick, Mr. Harrison married Emily Scott, a immaculate housekeeper. Their stark differences in domestic habits—especially regarding her excessive neatness and his swearing parrot, Ginger—led to a bitter separation. Leaving his wife behind, Mr. Harrison moved to Avonlea, Prince Edward Island, where he bought Robert Bell's farm next door to Green Gables and lived as a supposed bachelor. Initially gaining a reputation as an eccentric and irritable crank, he clashed with Anne Shirley after her Jersey cow trampled his oatfield, but the two quickly reconciled and became warm friends over tea and cake. He supported the Avonlea Village Improvement Society in his own gruff manner and offered Anne humorously frank advice on her writing and teaching. During a severe hail-and-thunder storm his house was struck by lightning and his beloved parrot Ginger was killed. Shortly thereafter, his wife Emily arrived at his farm, having discovered his whereabouts through a joke item in a Charlottetown newspaper; the couple reconciled and happily resumed their marriage. Following her arrival, Mr. Harrison became a tidy, well-shaved, church-going citizen of Avonlea, while maintaining his friendship with Anne and his unique, blunt outlook on life.

## Background by volume

- Lived formerly in Scottsford, New Brunswick, before moving to Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- Inherited his profane parrot, Ginger, from his deceased sailor brother  <sub>[v2 c3 P6](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0006), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c25 P58](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0058)</sub>
- Separated from his wife Emily due to domestic friction over household tidiness and his parrot  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057), [v2 c25 P58](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0058), [v2 c25 P59](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0059)</sub>
- Purchased Robert Bell's farm adjoining Green Gables in Avonlea  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>

## Quotes

> Bless my soul, this is the third time, miss . . . the third time! Patience has ceased to be a virtue, miss.  <sub>[v2 c1 P13](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0013)</sub>

> I’m a terrible outspoken old fellow, that’s all . . . awful apt to tell the truth, no matter if it is a bit plain.  <sub>[v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025)</sub>

> Mark my words, you’ll never manage the young fry unless you keep a rod in pickle for them. The thing is impossible.  <sub>[v2 c4 P38](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0038)</sub>

> I suppose I’ll get used to it after awhile, but it eases me up to look at the yard. Emily hasn’t had time to tidy it up yet.  <sub>[v2 c25 P55](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0055)</sub>

> Changes ain’t totally pleasant but they’re excellent things.  <sub>[v2 c30 P1](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0001)</sub>
